title: Owner-Item Hold on the Reconstruction Final Draw: Upgrades and Carrier-Denied Lines
content:
The owner-item hold on the final draw of a Reconstruction contract keeps out the owner's own items: the contract's signed owner upgrade change orders and, where the claim arrangement bills them to the customer, the amounts written off on the claim file as carrier-denied lines. The arrangement and the write-offs are those of the claim file kept under Insurance Claim Services.

**Carrier-funded.** A final draw is carrier-funded when its funding route, set by the base draw rule from the linked claim file, is not the customer: the claim file has a dwelling payment the carrier issued to the company directly (contractor direct), by a check naming the insured and the company (insured two-party), or into the mortgagee's loss-draft account (mortgagee loss draft). On any other final draw the customer funds the draw.

**Rule.** On a carrier-funded final draw:

- when the claim arrangement bills carrier-denied amounts to the customer, the hold is the amounts written off on the claim file as carrier-denied lines plus the amounts of the signed owner upgrade change orders;
- when the claim arrangement does not bill carrier-denied amounts to the customer, the hold is the amounts of the signed owner upgrade change orders.

On a final draw that is not carrier-funded there is no owner-item hold.

## Cases (hypothetical figures)

| Carrier-funded | Arrangement bills carrier-denied amounts to the customer | Carrier-denied write-offs | Signed owner upgrades | Owner-item hold |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | $740.00 | $1,860.00 | $2,600.00 |
| yes | no | $740.00 | $1,860.00 | $1,860.00 |
| no | any | any | any | none |
